Rules / Correctness

SK2015 throw ex; resets the stack trace

Re-throwing the caught exception by name restarts its stack trace at the throw.

CategoryCorrectness
Default severitywarning
ScopeSyntax
Needs a compilationno
Runs under --load=looseyes
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, safe
Language version floor—
Since0.8
ReSharperPossibleIntendedRethrow (resharper_possible_intended_rethrow_highlighting)

Why

throw ex; inside catch (Exception ex) assigns a fresh stack trace to the exception, so every frame between the original throw site and this catch is erased. The result is a production log that points at the handler rather than at the fault, which is the one piece of information the log existed to carry. throw; re-throws the same exception with its trace intact. The two forms look interchangeable and are not, which is why this is worth a rule rather than a review comment.

Example

Instead of:

try {
    Parse(input);
} catch (FormatException ex) {
    Log(ex);
    throw ex;
}

Write:

try {
    Parse(input);
} catch (FormatException ex) {
    Log(ex);
    throw;
}

When it does not fire

The rule fires only when the thrown expression is a bare identifier whose name is the identifier the nearest enclosing catch clause declares, and that name is never assigned anywhere inside the clause. Throwing a different exception, a wrapped exception, an exception belonging to an outer catch clause, a field, a parameter, or a variable the clause reassigned is not this pattern and is not reported. throw ex; inside a lambda, a local function or a nested catch clause within the block is excluded, because a bare throw; is either illegal or means something else there. ⚠ The fix drops the catch variable's name when the rewrite leaves it with no readers, so catch (FormatException ex) { throw ex; } becomes catch (FormatException) { throw; }. Without that second edit the repair introduces CS0168 — an unused variable — which a fixIsSafe: true rule may not do and which fails a build with TreatWarningsAsErrors. Where the clause still reads the name, in a when filter or before the throw, the name stays; where a clause holds two rewritable throws the deletion is carried by the last of them, so it happens once rather than twice over the same span.
